text: Morning. By nine o'clock, every seat is taken.
The Sun climbs over the walls, and the stone begins to burn. Thirty degrees. Then thirty-five.
There is no roof. No shade. Fifty thousand people, packed shoulder to shoulder.
Then you notice them, high up on the top of the wall. Sailors. Hundreds of them, sent from the Roman fleet.
They haul on ropes, tied to two hundred and forty wooden masts.
And slowly, a giant sail starts to slide out over the crowd.
The velarium. A roof made of cloth, big enough to shade most of the stands.
Down in the arena, the morning shows begin. Hunters, and wild animals from three continents.
You can't see it from here. But you can hear it. And you can feel fifty thousand people jump to their feet.
Noon. The heat is unbearable. You need water, and air, and a way out.
So you squeeze through the crowd, and take the first staircase you can find.
But it doesn't lead out. It leads down.
